pages.title: AssembleJS — Your frameworks. One application.
pages.description: Combine React, Vue, Svelte and other UI frameworks in one server-rendered application. Connect assemblies through page events and use the MCP server from your development tools.

pages.title: Create your first application — AssembleJS
pages.description: Run an AssembleJS page, then add the frameworks you want to use.

pages.title: Getting started — AssembleJS
pages.description: An assembly is a piece of a page written in one framework. A page places assemblies. That is the whole model, and the rest of this page is how you write one.

pages.title: Release notes — AssembleJS
pages.description: What is in each version of AssembleJS, newest first.

pages.title: Documentation — AssembleJS
pages.description: Build pages, connect data and deploy an AssembleJS application.

pages.title: The tutorial — AssembleJS
pages.description: One project, from nothing to a deployed server, in the order you would actually do it. Each step is one command or one file, and every file here is taken from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For React developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A React assembly is a component in a file whose name says it is React. The server renders it, the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold Svelte or Vue beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For Vue developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A Vue assembly is a single-file component. The server renders it, the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold React or Svelte beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For Svelte developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A Svelte assembly is a component, Svelte 5 and runes. The server renders it, the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold React or Vue beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For Preact developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A Preact assembly is a component in a file whose name says it is Preact. The server renders it, the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold React or Svelte beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its conformance fixtures, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For Solid developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A Solid assembly is a component in a file whose name says it is Solid, compiled by Solid's own compiler. The server renders it, the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold React or Vue beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For Lit developers — AssembleJS
pages.description: A Lit assembly is a view, cart.lit.ts, a function from the assembly's props to a Lit template, and the elements it places are yours. The server renders it, each element into a declarative shadow root; the browser hydrates it, and the page it sits on can hold React or Svelte beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its design document or its tests.

pages.title: For template authors — AssembleJS
pages.description: A template assembly is one file in EJS, Handlebars, Nunjucks, Pug or Markdown, rendered on the server by its own engine and nothing else; it ships no JavaScript unless a file beside it asks for some. The page it sits on can hold React or Svelte beside it. Everything on this page is from the repository's own examples, its conformance fixtures, its design document or its tests.

pages.description: Install AssembleJS and its framework renderers from npm.
